test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 29 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: We should use coal, petroleum and natural gas judiciously.
Coke, coal tar and coal gas are the products of coal.
Coal, petroleum and natural gas are fossil fuels.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Fossil fuels are inexhaustible resources**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fossil fuels**

 
 
• Non-renewable energy sources include any sort of energy or material that cannot be promptly renewed or replenished.
 
• Because they take hundreds or millions of years to develop, fossil fuels are considered non-renewable resources. They cannot be reused immediately after being consumed.
 
• Rock strata can build over the remnants of plants and animals. These are known as organic remnants by scientists.
 
• High pressures and temperatures can convert organic matter into three valuable commodities: coal, oil, and natural gas. Fossil fuels include coal, oil, and natural gas.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Renewable and nonrenewable resources are energy sources used by human society on a regular basis.
 
• The distinction between these two categories of resources is that renewable resources can replace themselves naturally, whereas nonrenewable resources cannot.
 
• This signifies that nonrenewable resources are finite and cannot be used indefinitely.
 
• Nonrenewable resources are classified into four categories: oil, natural gas, coal, and nuclear energy. Oil, natural gas, and coal are all examples of fossil fuels.
 
• Over millions of years, fossil fuels were produced within the Earth from dead plants and animals, hence the moniker "fossil" fuels. They are found in rock and sediment layers underground.
 
• The plant and animal leftovers were transformed into crude oil (also known as petroleum), coal, and natural gas by the combination of pressure and heat.
